Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

must 0.3.0

  • plot() of must_interactions objects has been redesigned and draws four kinds of figure, chosen with type:

    • "effects" (the new default): for each interaction, the effect of each stressor alone, the combined effect expected under the null model, the combined effect observed and the interaction, with its class at the right: how the interaction arises.
    • "interactions": the interactions alone, one row each, on the scale of the null model or as relative deviations (scale), optionally under headers by set, time or group (group_by).
    • "models": the interaction under each null model as a deviation relative to the reference, with its class: whether the conclusion depends on the null model.
    • "time": one figure per set with the single and combined effects and the interaction over the sampling times.

    Sets, times and groups are chosen with set_id, time and context; labels with labels, stressor_labels, label_style and label_width. Classes are written as codes (S+, S-, A+, A-, n.d.) or names (classes). Long figures are split into pages (per_page). Infinite estimates, estimates outside given limits and intervals cut by the limits end in arrows (type = "models" cuts intervals that reach far beyond the estimates). plot() returns the rows drawn invisibly, and arguments it does not use are now an error instead of being passed to plot.default().

  • estimate_interactions() no longer fails with glmmTMB 1.1.11 to 1.1.15 when two or more treatment combinations have only zeros (or only successes): vcov() of those versions fails for a model with two or more parameters fixed at the boundary, and the covariance of the fixed effects is now built from that of the estimated parameters.

  • Andreu Rico is now an author and copyright holder of the package: citation("must") and the methods written by report_interactions() cite both authors. The README and DESCRIPTION name the projects that fund must.

must 0.2.0

  • The package has a website, https://pabloamadorc.github.io/must/, with the help pages, the vignettes and the case studies.

  • Data: polazzo_zooplankton now has every taxon of the source (its eight columns are unchanged), and two new tables hold the other communities of that experiment (polazzo_phytoplankton, polazzo_macroinvertebrates). New data of Hermann et al. (2024), an outdoor mesocosm experiment with an insecticide (imidacloprid) and three temperature regimes (ambient, elevated and heatwaves): zooplankton, phytoplankton, macroinvertebrates, water quality, nutrients, leaf litter decomposition and imidacloprid concentrations (hermann_zooplankton and six more tables). Community tables have one column per taxon, with its name in the source file in the attribute "taxa".

  • New data of six experiments with different designs, from two to five stressors: drought and plant invasion on field plots in blocks (alba_arthropods), salinisation and nutrient enrichment in two orders (fuggle_biofilms), temperature, photoperiod and microbiome removal in two diatoms (giesler_diatoms), temperature, salinity and oxygen in horseshoe crab embryos (vasquez_embryos), four stressors on stream mesocosms fed by header tanks (hunn_invertebrates) and five global changes on split plots (niboyet_denitrification). The article “Case studies” of the package website reanalyses each of them.

  • New vignette, “Two mesocosm experiments” (vignette("mesocosms")): the whole workflow, from the design to the methods paragraph, on the phytoplankton and macroinvertebrates of Polazzo & Rico (2021) and the zooplankton, chironomids and leaf litter decomposition of Hermann et al. (2024), with baselines common to all stressors or per stressor, a density declared continuous, a taxon eliminated by a stressor, the null models suggested for each response and a test of equivalence.

  • New report_interactions(): writes the methods of an analysis from the settings of the output of estimate_interactions() and, if given, of classify_interactions() and compare_null_models(): the design, the model of each response and how its error distribution was chosen, the null models and why (the criteria of suggest_null_models() or a justification), how the interactions were estimated and tested, and how they were classified, with the works cited. A table lists every decision with the function and argument that control it, the value used, its default and its source (default, set by the user, chosen by must, estimated, suggested or recorded). format() gives plain text or markdown for R Markdown and Quarto documents. To support it, fit_responses() and estimate_interactions() record the versions of must, R and the packages used and whether the seed was given, estimate_interactions() keeps a summary of the models in settings$fit, and the outputs of classify_interactions() and compare_null_models() keep alpha (and the null models compared) as attributes.

  • New logo: the red hexagon with the name of the package, on a white background.

  • New suggest_null_models(): the guidelines of Schäfer & Piggott (2018, Fig. 3) for the choice of a null model, from whether the stressors act similarly, whether one acts specifically on physiology, whether the effect is mortality, whether the stressor-effect relationship or the distribution of sensitivities is known, how the sensitivities are correlated and how large the effects of the stressors alone are relative to the effect limit. Unknown criteria take every value, and all the null models they lead to are kept, with the steps that lead to each, why the others are excluded and which unknown criteria would change the choice. The effects can be given or estimated from a fitted model (also one fitted outside must) in every contrast set and time, from the cells with one stressor alone, with intervals: a criterion whose interval spans its threshold stays unknown. Stressors may increase the response: each effect has a direction and each set the interaction type of Piggott et al. (2015); concentration addition needs effects in the same direction and the stress addition model no increase; and for a proportion that the stressors increase, the guidelines are applied to its complement, on which the interactions are then estimated. estimate_interactions() takes the result as null_models, checks its sensitivity and keeps its criteria and reasons in settings$null_model_choice.

  • describe_design() gains shared, for rows that belong to every group of a by column: a control common to two exposure regimes, to two orders of application of the stressors, or to upstream and downstream ponds. Those rows enter the analysis once and supply the cells that each group lacks, instead of being copied into every group. fit_responses() and estimate_interactions() (also for models fitted outside must) use them in the sets of each group; set_cells gives the group in which each cell was observed.

  • baseline in describe_design() can be a named list with the times before each stressor was applied, for stressors that started later than others (drying started after the warming and shading treatments): an interaction is not estimated before all of its stressors were applied, and the interactions among the other stressors are. With time_structure = "additive", those samplings are coded with the stressors not yet applied at their control.

  • describe_design() lists as missing, within each by group, only the combinations of the levels used in that group, and checks the labels of the treatments: levels that differ only in letter case or spaces (“control” and “Control”) and labels that are not valid UTF-8 text (a file read with the wrong encoding) give a warning, and levels of a stressor observed in only some by groups, which may be one treatment under two labels, are pointed out.

  • describe_design() has been checked on 36 published experiments with very different designs, which motivated the changes above.

  • Equivalence: estimate_interactions() gains margin (no default), the largest negligible deviation as a share of the response of the reference cell. Every interaction now has its relative deviation, (observed − expected) / reference, the same quantity for every null model (relative, relative_lower, relative_upper); with a margin it is also tested for equivalence with two one-sided tests (p_equivalence, p_equivalence_adjusted), each from the distance to the margin on a scale on which the variance of a mean does not depend on the mean (the same with both inference methods). classify_interactions() (verdict) and summary() combine both tests into four verdicts: deviation, negligible deviation, equivalent and inconclusive, so that “additive” can be a claim rather than a failure to detect a deviation.

  • fit_responses() no longer chooses between the Poisson and the negative binomial by AIC for counts with its default candidates: it fits the negative binomial and uses the Poisson only if that does not converge, as happens when the counts show no overdispersion (reason says so). With overdispersed counts and four units per combination, the AIC chose the Poisson in a fifth of simulated experiments, and the residual checks did not exclude it, so the tests rejected true null models too often (7% at a nominal 5%); with the new rule they stayed at 5–6%. Candidates given in families are still chosen by AIC.

  • For a glm() whose dispersion is estimated (quasi-Poisson, quasi-binomial and the other families except Poisson and binomial), estimate_interactions() now uses a t distribution with its residual degrees of freedom, as summary.glm() does; emmeans gives such models infinite degrees of freedom, which made their tests reject a true null model too often with few units. Results for these models change.

  • New compare_null_models(): for each interaction estimated under two or more null models, whether all of them flag a deviation with the same sign ("robust"), only some ("model_dependent"), none ("none") or some in opposite directions ("conflicting"), with what each null model flags. summary() counts these cases when there are two or more null models.

  • The default of null_models in estimate_interactions() is now "AD" (it was c("AD", "MU", "DO")): in simulated experiments generated without interaction by five mechanisms (AD, MU or BL, DO, SAM and CA), AD flagged the fewest false interactions on average among the null models that two-level factorials can test, under a rule fixed before the simulations (see “Default null model” in ?estimate_interactions and vignette("must")). null_models = c("AD", "MU", "DO") gives the previous results. The simulation script, the rates of every scenario and the report are installed in system.file("simulations", package = "must").

  • estimate_interactions() gains the Bliss independence null model (null_models = "BL"; Bliss 1939): single and combined effects relative to the reference cell, the net interaction wK - prod(wi) and, for three stressors, the emergent interaction of Beppler et al. (2016), with its rescaled value (rescaled) and the descriptive class of Beppler et al. (rescaled_class). As for the other null models, a deviation is judged from the interval and the p-value; the cut-offs only describe its size. The emergent interaction is not_defined for four or more stressors.

  • estimate_interactions() is now generic and also analyses models fitted outside must (lm(), glm(), mgcv::gam(), lme4::glmer(), glmmTMB::glmmTMB() and the other models supported by emmeans), given the output of describe_design() for their data. The means of the treatment combinations are those of emmeans, the degrees of freedom those that emmeans gives or those set in the new df argument, and diagnostics$means lists the means used. Quantities that the model fixes at zero are not_applicable, and means that the model cannot estimate or that lie at the boundary of its link make their contrasts not_estimable. emmeans is a suggested package.

  • Two more null models from ecotoxicology: the stress addition model (null_models = "SAM"; Liess et al. 2016), whose beta distribution of stress capacity is set with sam_shape, and concentration addition ("CA", Loewe additivity), which fits a log-logistic dose-response curve to the doses of each stressor tested alone and needs at least two of them. Both give the net interaction on the scale relative to the reference cell.

  • classify_interactions() also classifies the BL, SAM and CA interactions.

must 0.1.0

First public release.

  • describe_design() reports, before any model is fitted, the observed and missing treatment combinations, the contrast sets the design identifies (net deviation and, for three or more stressors, the pure highest-order interaction), cells shared by several sets, the replication unit, subsamples, repeated measures and unbalanced sampling. With groups it reports the stressors applied to whole groups of units (blocks, whole plots, rooms) and flags the contrast sets confounded with differences among groups. baseline declares pre-treatment sampling times, and background = "all" adds contrast sets with the other stressors at their non-control levels.
  • fit_responses() fits a cell-means GLMM with glmmTMB to one or several responses and selects the error distribution by convergence, DHARMa residual checks and AIC. It handles numbers of successes out of a number of trials (trials), counts per unit of sampling effort (offset), one dispersion per by group or per treatment combination (dispersion) and treatment combinations with only zeros (or only successes), whose means are fixed at the boundary of the link. Random intercepts for repeated units and estimable groups are added automatically, and removed when their variance is estimated at zero.
  • estimate_interactions() computes single, combined and interaction effects under the simple addition (AD), multiplicative (MU) and dominance (DO) null models, with Krinsky–Robb simulation or the delta method and adjusted p-values. By default it corrects for small samples (REML covariance and t distributions with the degrees of freedom of the experimental units); correction = "none" gives the asymptotic procedure of Madge Pimentel et al. (2025). Contrasts that involve a combination with only zeros are tested from the probability of that outcome under the null model, and designs with several sampling times also get the average of each effect over the times.
  • classify_interactions() applies the directional classification of Piggott et al. (2015) under AD and MU, extended to sets of three or more stressors.
  • summary() and plot() methods for must_interactions objects, the example data set polazzo_zooplankton and citation("must").
